conflicts.name: 2026 Iran war (US and Israel vs Iran)
conflicts.started: 2026-02-28 (US Operation Epic Fury and Israeli Operation Roaring Lion; current phase since ceasefire collapse on 2026-07-08)
conflicts.summary: A US-Israeli air war on Iran that began on 28 February 2026 killed Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei and much of Iran's security leadership. Iran answered with thousands of missiles and drones at Israel, US bases and every Gulf monarchy, and closed the Strait of Hormuz. A June peace memorandum collapsed in July, and by late October the two sides are in an armed stand-off with no ceasefire and threats of a second round after the US midterms.

conflicts.name: Israel-Hamas war in Gaza (ceasefire phase)
conflicts.started: 2025-10-10 (ceasefire phase of the war that began 2023-10-07)
conflicts.summary: A US-brokered ceasefire has stopped full-scale war in Gaza since 10 October 2025 and returned all hostages, but Israel holds a growing share of the Strip behind the 'Yellow Line' and conducts near-daily strikes. Phase two, which trades Hamas disarmament for further Israeli withdrawal and an international force, is deadlocked.

zones.note: Largest population concentration; frequent Israeli strikes on operatives; building collapse killed 20+ on 16 Sep 2026.

conflicts.name: Israel-Hezbollah war in Lebanon (2026)
conflicts.summary: Hezbollah reopened fire on 2 March 2026 after the US-Israeli war on Iran began, and Israel answered with its deepest invasion of Lebanon in a generation, crossing the Litani and taking Beaufort. Since a 19 June ceasefire Israel holds a 570-600 sq km 'security zone' behind its own Yellow Line, while a US-brokered Israel-Lebanon framework asks the Lebanese army to disarm Hezbollah zone by zone.

conflicts.name: Russia-Ukraine long-range strike war
conflicts.summary: Both sides wage a nightly long-range war. Russia fires hundreds of drones, increasingly jet-powered, plus ballistic and cruise missiles at Ukraine's power grid, cities and ports, while Ukraine hits Russian refineries, arms plants, airbases and ships up to 2,300 km away. Civilian casualties in Ukraine hit a multi-year high in September 2026.

zones.name: Kyiv
zones.note: Main target of Russia's largest 2026 combined strikes, including Oreshnik on 24 May; civilian casualties on 22 of 30 days in September 2026.

zones.name: Kharkiv
zones.note: Daily drone and glide-bomb strikes, including double-tap strikes on rescuers; 280,000 customers lost power on 16 October 2026.

zones.note: Russian strikes on ports and ships cut traffic from about 400 ships in July to fewer than 10 in September 2026.

zones.note: Oreshnik strike on the Lviv aviation repair plant on 8 January 2026; Volyn grid strikes in October.

zones.name: Sea of Azov

zones.name: Russian border belt: Belgorod, Kursk, Bryansk, Voronezh, Oryol, Lipetsk
zones.note: Ukrainian strikes on radars, airbases (Borisoglebsk), power plants and defence-electronics factories.

conflicts.name: Russia-Ukraine war (ground war)
conflicts.summary: Europe's largest war since 1945 entered its fifth year with Russia still attacking along a roughly 1,200 km front but gaining almost nothing in 2026. Russia took Pokrovsk, Myrnohrad, Siversk and Huliaipole in late 2025, then stalled; Ukraine counterattacked in the south from February and north of Lyman from September. ISW assesses Russia has been net losing ground since 1 September 2026, while the battle for Kostiantynivka grinds on a year after it began.

conflicts.name: Syrian internal conflicts (government vs SDF, Druze Sweida, Alawite coast, ISIS)
conflicts.summary: Damascus crushed the Kurdish-led SDF in a three-week offensive in January 2026, absorbed its forces and saw it formally dissolve in August, and the US then left Syria. The remaining fighting is an armed standoff with Israeli-backed Druze forces around Sweida, a reduced ISIS insurgency, and sectarian violence around the Alawite coast and Homs.

conflicts.name: Yemen war (Houthi-Saudi war, Red Sea attacks and southern crisis)
conflicts.started: 2026-07-13 (collapse of the 2022 Saudi-Houthi truce; southern STC crisis from 2025-12-02)
conflicts.summary: Yemen's war reignited in 2026 on two levels. In the south, Saudi-backed forces crushed the UAE-backed Southern Transitional Council in January after it seized the east. In the north, the Houthis joined the Iran war in March, broke their 2022 truce with Saudi Arabia in July, blockaded Saudi shipping, hit southern Saudi cities, and seized Yemen's Red Sea coast up to Bab al-Mandeb in September, while the government launched a counter-offensive in October.

US troops left Iraq on 30 September 2026, and Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi is trying to disarm the militias by mid-2027, with Kataib Hezbollah and Nujaba refusing.

conflicts.name: Strait of Hormuz crisis and Gulf tanker war
conflicts.started: 2026-02-28 (Iranian closure; current phase since 2026-07-08 collapse of the Islamabad Memorandum)
conflicts.summary: Since 28 February 2026 Iran has kept the Strait of Hormuz effectively closed with fast boats, mines, missiles, drones, jamming and seizures, letting through only ships it approves and charging tolls. The US answered with its own blockade of Iranian ports, strikes on the IRGC Navy and mine clearance. October 2026 is the most violent month for shipping since March, with mine strikes on supertankers and sinkings, and traffic down from about 85 ships a day to a handful.
